html:
The campaign in which the Han Empire of China conquered the kingdom of Nanyue in 111 BCE. Nanyue covered what are now Guangdong, Guangxi and northern Vietnam, and its fall began about a thousand years of Chinese rule over the Red River delta.

Nanyue had been founded in 204 BCE by Zhao Tuo, a Qin general who made himself king in the far south, with his capital at Panyu, today's Guangzhou. His heirs accepted Han overlordship in name. In 112 BCE the minister Lü Jia killed the young king, his Chinese born mother and the Han envoys, who were arranging for Nanyue to join the empire. Emperor Wu sent armies by land and river, and Panyu fell the next year.

The Han split the land into commanderies, including Jiaozhi in the Red River delta. Chinese rule there was resisted many times, most famously in the Trưng sisters' rebellion of 40 CE, and it lasted until 938, when the victory at Bạch Đằng opened the way for the independent kingdom later called Đại Việt.
